name: context-os
description: Stop Claude burning your tokens re-exploring your own code every session. context-os maps your repo into small, portable context files — one per folder plus a root index — that Claude (or Codex, or Gemini) reads on demand instead of re-scanning your whole project. And the saving is bigger than it looks: reading a file isn't charged once, because everything already in the conversation gets re-processed on every message you send after it. On one real 5,328-message session, 71% of all token cost was re-reading the conversation so far, and reading 30,000 tokens of source at message 100 cost 524x its apparent size. Swapping a big source read for a small map read doesn't save you once — it saves you on every message that follows. It maps what matters: it ranks folders and deeply maps only the strategic ones (the code hubs and entry points), keeps a cheap skeleton for the rest, and folds pure docs/data folders into their parent — instead of blindly mapping every folder. Or go fully lazy: map the whole repo as free skeletons once, then /context-os-catchup enriches only the folders you actually worked in this session, so enrichment cost tracks real use. It keeps the maps honest: a drift check flags a map the moment its folder's code changes, so a stale map warns you instead of quietly lying. And /relay writes the handoff before you stop — the one next action, what done looks like, what not to redo, and the paths to reuse — then hands it to a reader that knows nothing about your project and may open nothing else, which scores 0-10 whether it could actually resume from it; below 8 you fix the file while you still can, because a handoff can only be repaired while the context that would repair it still exists. Six commands (/context-os, /context-os-catchup, /context-os-update, /context-os-status, /relay, /snapshot), a folder ranker, sharded per-folder enrichment agents with a self-healing repair loop, a drift-detection hook, and three honest, separate numbers that are never merged: a token-save ceiling measured against your real source, a per-session measurement of what map use actually delivered (a hook logs whether the agent read the map or re-read the source), and a cost profile read from the real per-message usage Claude Code already records for you. It also lets an agent retrieve the exact original behind any map reference (compress-cache-retrieve), exposes the maps + retrieval over an MCP server so any agent or proxy can consume them, and now maps config/docs/data folders too — not just code. Because maps are meant to be committed, what goes in one is enforced in code: never a secret (the .env family and anything your .gitignore excludes are skipped, and config/log files are described by shape, never contents), never an instruction (agents read maps before source, so text that drifted in from a dependency's README would act as a command — the audit fails on it), never a file outside your project, and never a node that doesn't trace to real code. It also never touches your existing CLAUDE.md beyond its own marked block. Free, offline, $0, no server, no API keys, stdlib-only.
